terms.grammar: pronoun: the ordinary forms of tū, used reflexively
terms.comment: As with “myself”, there is no separate reflexive: tē servā, save yourself; tēcum, with yourself. Often no pronoun at all: “look after yourself” is cūrā ut valeās.

evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.2.33: ut tē ipsum servēs
Cic. Fam. 9.14.8: fac ut dīligentissimē tē ipsum custōdiās (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse)
terms.comment: Agrees with tū when it stresses the doer (tūte ipse, you did it yourself), with tē when it stresses the object: ut tē ipsum servēs, to save yourself (and not something else).

terms.gloss: you yourself, you and no one else
evidence: Enn. in Gell. 2.29.20: quod tūte agere possiēs

phrases.latin: ut tē ipsum servēs, nōn expergīsceris?
phrases.english: Won’t you wake up to save yourself?

phrases.latin: Tūte hoc intrīstī: tibi omne est exedendum.
phrases.english: You cooked this up yourself: you must eat it all up.

phrases.latin: cūrā ut valeās et nōs amēs et tibi persuādeās tē ā mē frāternē amārī
phrases.english: Look after yourself, love us, and be sure that I love you like a brother.

phrases.latin: hoc erit tibi argūmentum semper in prōmptū situm: nē quid expectēs amīcōs, quod tūte agere possiēs
phrases.english: Keep this lesson always at hand: don’t expect your friends to do what you can do yourself.

phrases.latin: fac ut dīligentissimē tē ipsum custōdiās
phrases.english: Take the greatest care of yourself.

sources: Lewis & Short: tu · Lewis & Short: ipse · Lewis & Short: tute
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-epistulae, loci-gellius, loci-horatius, loci-terentius), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
